decisive_items: A clinical diagnosis of a nonspecific chronic abscess with buccal-space involvement was made
The lesion shelled out easily, with no involvement of buccinator muscle or bone
creamish-brown, firm, irregular, and had a leathery pouch-like appearance
response.rationale: Chronic buccal space abscess is directly stated and best matches the recurrent indolent swelling, CT cystic loculations with dense content, and fibrous leathery pouch that shelled out; R4 is only a distant runner-up because the buccal location and abscess imaging are present, but staphylococcal etiology is unconfirmed.

rejected.why: Tuberculous abscess lacks TB symptoms, lymphadenopathy, or granulomatous pathology; leathery pouch is nonspecific.
Staphylococcal infection has no organism isolation and lacks buccal-space specificity.
Odontogenic source is unsupported; surgery confirmed no bone involvement and the lesion was entirely soft tissue.
Actinomycosis lacks sinus tracts, sulfur granules, or culture confirmation; chronic abscess features are nonspecific.
Diabetic cheilitis is irrelevant; no lip or cheilitis findings and diabetes does not explain the buccal mass.
